Earlier this year, Apple significantly raised prices due to the ongoing global memory shortage. For example, the iPad Air went from $599 to $749, the M5 MacBook Pro from $1,699 to $1,999, and Apple TV from $129 to $199. These are just some examples — the key point is that this round of price increases is quite staggering.

This situation raises the question — will Apple bring major improvements to its products under the new pricing to attract consumers?

Of course, some Apple products are getting major refreshes soon, with the MacBook Pro and iPad mini being two examples. But for products without significant updates in the short term, I really can't imagine how Apple can continue to sell "yesterday's technology" at high prices while still making consumers feel it's a great deal — especially given the current state of the second-hand market.

If you could buy an M4 iPad Air for $599 (or even as low as $499) just a few months ago, why pay $749 now? This argument becomes even more apparent with higher-priced products.

Some Apple products haven't seen major changes for quite a while. The iPad Air has used the same design and features since 2020, with only chip upgrades and Apple Pencil Pro support. The entry-level iPad has remained largely unchanged since 2022, and the iMac has been roughly the same from 2021 until now.

Do these products need a redesign? Not necessarily. But I think Apple could do something to make existing products at current prices more attractive. For example, the iMac could switch to a miniLED display, the iPad Air could support a 120Hz refresh rate, or the entry-level iPad could feature a fully laminated display.

Compared to the magnitude of the price increases, the cost of these upgrades would be relatively low, but should make consumers feel more comfortable about their purchases. On the other hand, Apple might also cut some product specs to offset the price hikes. For example, we might see the return of the 128GB iPhone.

What are your thoughts on Apple's product lineup after the price increases? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
